label: late-original / <DEL> step, specific input tokens, in sequences starting with p/a/k-like tokens
explanation: Fires only while reading the input: on original tokens from t>=2 (rate climbs with position, about 24% at orig_idx 8) and on the <DEL> step (20% of delimiter steps, 31% of mass). Almost never fires in the copy phase (0.1% of mass) and never at t=0/1. Within that window it behaves like a graded accumulator that depends on two things. (1) The current input: n, x, u, i, h, g, 2, v, w and <DEL> have elevated rates; common letters such as o and l do not. (2) The first original token: sequences starting with p or a (3.5x lift), and to a lesser degree k, m, b, y, j, f, carry most of the mass. Highest activations (about 1.0 of max) are late-original-phase n/x/h/u/2 tokens and <DEL> in sequences starting with p or a. First occurrences of a token account for 93% of the mass. The conjunction gets dev F1 0.57 and mass recall 0.63. Because it is a soft additive dependence on many tokens, a boolean predicate misses a lot and also has many false positives: phase<=1 & t>=3 & token set alone gives recall 0.80 but precision 0.27.
